body.statement: Can the contact-set multiplier handle be developed into a confidence set that retains uniform \((1-\alpha)\) coverage over \(\mathcal M_\eta\), has asymptotically exact rather than conservative coverage whenever the limiting contact-set Gaussian maximum has a continuous quantile, is first-order no wider than \(\mathcal C_n\) at every law with unique separated lower and upper simplex branches, and is strictly narrower on a nonempty observable region where inactive scores from \(\widetilde f_\beta^-\) and \(\widetilde f_\beta^+\) enlarge the all-branch Gaussian quantile?
body.justification: The all-branch envelope buys robustness by paying a potentially avoidable width cost away from ties.
body.gap: Fang and Santos (2019) motivates estimated contact derivatives, but uniform adaptation across this two-endpoint rational frontier with singular scores is not settled by the cited results.
body.consumer: A successful construction would deliver shorter sensitivity intervals on a certified regular region without sacrificing protection near branch switches.
